title: Getting Started with Hugging Face Diffusers
summary: Set up Hugging Face Diffusers with SDXL, generate images, tune settings, reduce GPU memory use, and serve a FastAPI endpoint to your JavaScript app.
body_markdown:
Hugging Face Diffusers is a Python library for running image, video and audio diffusion models on your own hardware. It packages the text encoder, scheduler, denoising network and VAE into a single pipeline object that you call with a prompt.


Hosted image APIs are easy to start with. Then the per-image bills arrive, rate limits slow down your prototype, and you want to know what the model is actually doing. Running the model locally fixes all three, but most tutorials assume you already know PyTorch.


This guide is written for JavaScript developers. It takes you from installation to a first image, explains the settings that matter, shows how to fit the model on smaller GPUs, and finishes with a FastAPI endpoint that your frontend calls with` fetch()` . The examples target Diffusers v0.42.1.


## Key Takeaways


- Load` stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0` with` DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(..., dtype=torch.float16)` and move it to` "cuda"` on NVIDIA GPUs or` "mps"` on Apple Silicon.
- SDXL base 1.0 is released under the CreativeML Open RAIL++-M License. Read it before you ship generated images.
- A seeded` torch.Generator` makes outputs repeatable, so you can change one setting at a time and see its effect.
- If the model doesn’t fit in GPU memory, call` enable_model_cpu_offload()` first. The Diffusers docs describe sequential CPU offload as extremely slow.
- Load the pipeline once when the server starts and reuse it for every request. Never load it inside a request handler.


## What Is Hugging Face Diffusers?


[Diffusers](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/index) is Hugging Face’s library for diffusion models. Its central abstraction is` DiffusionPipeline` , which bundles the components a model needs:


- one or more text encoders that turn the prompt into embeddings
- a scheduler that controls the denoising algorithm
- a UNet or diffusion transformer that predicts the noise at each step
- a VAE that decodes the result into pixels


If you’re new to the Hub, Inference Providers or Spaces, read[A Quick Guide to Hugging Face for Developers](https://blog.openreplay.com/quick-guide-hugging-face-developers/) first. If you want inference with no Python backend at all,[Transformers.js runs models directly in the browser](https://blog.openreplay.com/run-ai-models-browser-transformers-js/) , although it covers a different set of models.


## What Hardware Does Diffusers Need?


Diffusers runs on three kinds of machine. An NVIDIA GPU is the fastest by a wide margin, an Apple Silicon Mac works through PyTorch’s` "mps"` backend, and a plain CPU works but is very slow.


Hardware Device string dtype What to expect


NVIDIA GPU` "cuda"`` torch.float16` Fast


Apple Silicon Mac` "mps"`` torch.float16` Works, slower than a discrete NVIDIA GPU


CPU only` "cpu"`` torch.float32` Works, very slow


The[Quickstart](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/quicktour) lists` "cuda"` ,` "mps"` ,` "xpu"` and` "cpu"` as device targets. Diffusers also has a dedicated[Apple Silicon (MPS) guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/optimization/mps) . This helper picks the right device and dtype for the current machine:


```text
import   torch


if   torch.cuda.is_available():
device, dtype   =   "  cuda  "  , torch.float16
elif   torch.backends.mps.is_available():
device, dtype   =   "  mps  "  , torch.float16
else  :
device, dtype   =   "  cpu  "  , torch.float32
```


## Install Diffusers and Generate a First Image


Generating a first image with Hugging Face Diffusers takes three steps: install Diffusers with PyTorch, load SDXL, then call the pipeline with a prompt and save` .images\[0\]` .


Diffusers[requires Python 3.11 or newer](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/releases/tag/v0.42.0) since v0.42.0, and is tested with PyTorch 2.6 or newer. Follow the[installation guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/installation) to set up a virtual environment, then install the packages. SDXL’s text encoders are CLIP models from Transformers, so install that library as well:


```text
uv   pip   install   "  diffusers[torch]>=0.42.1  "   transformers
# or: pip install "diffusers[torch]>=0.42.1" transformers
```


Using the` device` and` dtype` from the helper above, generate an image:


```text
import   torch
from   diffusers   import   DiffusionPipeline


pipeline   =   DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
"  stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0  "  ,
dtype  =  dtype,
).to(device)


prompt   =   "  isometric pixel-art coffee shop at dusk, warm window light, rain on the street  "
image   =   pipeline(prompt).images[  0  ]
image.save(  "  first.png  "  )
```


` image` is a PIL image, so` .save()` writes a PNG to disk. The model id is the checkpoint’s full Hub name, including the` stabilityai/` organization prefix.


**Licence:**[SDXL base 1.0](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0) is released under the[CreativeML Open RAIL++-M License](https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0/blob/main/LICENSE.md) . Read it before you use generated images in a product, and check the licence of any other model you swap in.


## Which SDXL Settings Matter Most?


Four SDXL pipeline arguments control most of what you see in the output:` num_inference_steps` ,` guidance_scale` ,` generator` , and` height` /` width` . Fix the seed first, then change one argument at a time.


```text
generator   =   torch.Generator().manual_seed(  42  )


image   =   pipeline(
prompt,
num_inference_steps  =  30  ,
guidance_scale  =  7.0  ,
height  =  1024  ,
width  =  1024  ,
generator  =  generator,
).images[  0  ]
```


- **` num_inference_steps`** sets how many denoising passes run. More steps take longer and usually add detail, until the gains level off.
- **` guidance_scale`** sets how closely the model follows the prompt. Higher values stick closer to the text, and values that are too high can look overcooked.
- **` generator`** fixes the starting noise. With the same model, settings and hardware, a seeded generator gives you the same image again.
- **` height` /` width`** set the output size in pixels. Larger images need more memory and more time.


The[SDXL pipeline reference](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/api/pipelines/stable_diffusion/stable_diffusion_xl) lists every argument along with its default value.


## Swap the Scheduler


The scheduler decides how noise is removed at each step, and different schedulers trade speed against quality. Replace it on a loaded pipeline with` from_config()` , passing in the existing config so the settings that match the checkpoint stay aligned:


```text
from   diffusers   import   DPMSolverMultistepScheduler


pipeline.scheduler   =   DPMSolverMultistepScheduler.from_config(pipeline.scheduler.config)


generator   =   torch.Generator().manual_seed(  42  )
image   =   pipeline(prompt,   num_inference_steps  =  20  ,   generator  =  generator).images[  0  ]
```


The[Schedulers guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/using-diffusers/schedulers) uses this exact pattern with SDXL. The[DPMSolverMultistepScheduler reference](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/api/schedulers/multistep_dpm_solver) states that it produces high-quality samples in around 20 steps. Keep the seed fixed when you compare schedulers, so the scheduler is the only thing that changes between the two images.


## How Do You Fit SDXL on Smaller GPUs?


If SDXL hits out-of-memory errors, try these four Diffusers memory fixes in order: model CPU offload, VAE tiling, VAE slicing and 4-bit quantization. Each step saves more memory and costs more speed.


1. **Model CPU offload.** Skip` .to(device)` and call` pipeline.enable_model_cpu_offload()` . Each whole model sits on the GPU only while it runs.
2. **VAE tiling.**` pipeline.vae.enable_tiling()` decodes large images in tiles. The[memory guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/optimization/memory) notes that this can cause slight tone variation between tiles.
3. **VAE slicing.**` pipeline.vae.enable_slicing()` decodes a batch one image at a time. It only helps when you generate several images in a single call.
4. **4-bit quantization.** Install` bitsandbytes` and add a short config:


```text
from   diffusers.quantizers   import   PipelineQuantizationConfig


quant_config   =   PipelineQuantizationConfig(
quant_backend  =  "  bitsandbytes_4bit  "  ,
quant_kwargs  =  {  "  load_in_4bit  "  :   True  ,   "  bnb_4bit_quant_type  "  :   "  nf4  "  ,   "  bnb_4bit_compute_dtype  "  : torch.float16},
components_to_quantize  =  [  "  unet  "  ],
)
pipeline   =   DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
"  stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0  "  ,
dtype  =  torch.float16,
quantization_config  =  quant_config,
)
pipeline.enable_model_cpu_offload()
```


The[quantization overview](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/quantization/overview) documents` PipelineQuantizationConfig` and its backends. Diffusers[added bitsandbytes quantization on MPS](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/releases/tag/v0.39.0) in v0.39.0, so this approach isn’t limited to CUDA. On Apple Silicon, bitsandbytes needs PyTorch 2.9 or newer, which is higher than the PyTorch 2.6 baseline above.


Avoid` enable_sequential_cpu_offload()` unless nothing else fits. It saves the most memory, but the memory guide calls it extremely slow. Also, a pipeline loaded with` device_map` must call` reset_device_map()` before you use` .to()` or either offload method.


## Calling Hugging Face Diffusers From a Web App


To use Diffusers from a frontend, wrap the pipeline in a small HTTP server. The server should load the model once at startup and return PNG bytes. Install` fastapi` and` uvicorn` , then save this as` main.py` :


```text
import   io, threading
from   contextlib   import   asynccontextmanager
import   torch
from   diffusers   import   DiffusionPipeline
from   fastapi   import   FastAPI, Response
from   fastapi.middleware.cors   import   CORSMiddleware
from   pydantic   import   BaseModel


state   =   {}
lock   =   threading.Lock()


@  asynccontextmanager
async   def   lifespan  (  app  : FastAPI):
state[  "  pipe  "  ]   =   DiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained(
"  stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0  "  ,   dtype  =  torch.float16
).to(  "  cuda  "  )    # or "mps"
yield
state.clear()


app   =   FastAPI(  lifespan  =  lifespan)
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware,   allow_origins  =  [  "  http://localhost:5173  "  ],
allow_methods  =  [  "  POST  "  ],   allow_headers  =  [  "  *  "  ])


class   GenerateRequest  (  BaseModel  ):
prompt:   str
seed:   int   |   None   =   None


@  app  .  post  (  "  /generate  "  )
def   generate  (  req  : GenerateRequest):
gen   =   torch.Generator().manual_seed(req.seed)   if   req.seed   is   not   None   else   None
with   lock:
image   =   state[  "  pipe  "  ](req.prompt,   generator  =  gen).images[  0  ]
buf   =   io.BytesIO()
image.save(buf,   format  =  "  PNG  "  )
return   Response(  content  =  buf.getvalue(),   media_type  =  "  image/png  "  )
```


Run it with` uvicorn main:app` . The code is built from three FastAPI features:


- The[lifespan handler](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/events/) loads the model once, before the server accepts any requests.` from_pretrained()` is far too slow to call per request.
- Because` generate` is a plain` def` , FastAPI[runs it in a threadpool](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/async/) instead of blocking the event loop.
- The lock makes requests use the GPU one at a time.


[CORSMiddleware](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/cors/) allows your dev frontend’s origin to call the endpoint.


On the frontend, use[fetch()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/fetch) to request the image, read the body as a Blob and display it with[URL.createObjectURL()](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/URL/createObjectURL_static) :


```text
async   function   generate  (  prompt  ,   seed  ,   img  ) {
const   res   =   await   fetch  (  "  http://localhost:8000/generate  "  , {
method  :   "  POST  "  ,
headers  :   {   "  Content-Type  "  :   "  application/json  "   },
body  :   JSON  .  stringify  ({   prompt  ,   seed   }),
});
if (  !  res  .  ok  )   throw   new   Error  (  `  Generation failed:   ${  res  .  status  }`  );
if (  img  .  src  .  startsWith  (  "  blob:  "  ))   URL  .  revokeObjectURL  (  img  .  src  );
img  .  src   =   URL  .  createObjectURL  (  await   res  .  blob  ());
}
```


Generation takes seconds, not milliseconds. Show a loading state, disable the submit button while a request is in flight, and pass an` AbortController` signal if users can cancel. Before you serve the generated PNGs to real visitors, shrink them with the[OpenReplay image compressor](https://openreplay.com/tools/image-compressor/) .


## Next Steps


Once the pipeline is loaded on the right device, Diffusers needs very little code: a model id, a dtype, a prompt and a seed. Generate a first image with SDXL, fix the seed and adjust one setting at a time. If memory runs short, work through the offload and quantization steps in order. Then put the FastAPI endpoint behind your frontend. From there, the memory guide and the Schedulers guide cover the trade-offs that come up as you tune for production.


## FAQs


Where does Diffusers store downloaded model weights?


from_pretrained() saves model files in the Hugging Face Hub cache and reuses them on later runs, so it does not download them again. The cache defaults to ~/.cache/huggingface/hub. Set the HF_HUB_CACHE environment variable to move only the model cache. Set HF_HOME to move all Hugging Face data, which places the cache at HF_HOME/hub. You can also pass a cache_dir argument to choose a location for a single load.


Why does the same seed give a different image on another machine?


A seed only fully reproduces an image on the same hardware with the same PyTorch version. CUDA GPUs use a different random number generator from CPUs, and GPU matrix multiplication is less deterministic. The Diffusers reproducibility guide recommends passing a CPU generator when results must match, which is what torch.Generator() creates by default. Even so, it does not promise identical output across different GPU models or PyTorch versions.


Does 4-bit bitsandbytes quantization work on an Apple Silicon Mac?


Yes, with recent versions. Diffusers added bitsandbytes quantization on MPS in v0.39.0, and bitsandbytes 0.50.0 made all of its 4-bit and LLM.int8() configurations work on MPS. The bitsandbytes MPS path needs PyTorch 2.9 or newer, which is higher than the PyTorch 2.6 minimum for Diffusers. On macOS 26 and later, installing the kernels package enables faster Metal kernels.
